sentences.text: Pretrained LLMs are good at text completion but struggle with following specific instructions, which is why instruction fine-tuning is used to make them better at responding to instructions.

If you are comfortable with PyTorch training loops, data loaders, and transfer-learning conventions from the previous chapter, you already have most of the practical setup; where this chapter adds new ideas, it will make the data shape and training target explicit before moving into evaluation.
We begin by clarifying why instruction fine-tuning is needed, what the instruction dataset contains, and how instruction, input, and output records are converted into Alpaca-style prompts.

Next, we walk through tokenization, variable-length sequences, per-batch padding with the end-of-text token, shifted targets for next-token prediction, ignoring padding in the loss with "-100", and the complete batching recipe, including optional masking choices.

From there, we load pretrained GPT-2 weights, map those parameters into the model, check the model before fine-tuning, and then close by evaluating a fine-tuned model with examples, response extraction, broader benchmarking ideas such as MMLU, automated judging with "Ollama" and "Llama 3", and practical directions for improving results.
Pretrained LLMs can complete text well, but they do not follow specific instructions well enough on their own, which is why instruction fine-tuning is needed.
Instruction fine-tuning uses examples made of instructions and desired responses, and some examples also include an additional input field.
The dataset used here has 1,100 instruction-input-output entries from various fields, and its purpose is to teach the model to follow instructions correctly.

Before fine-tuning, each dataset entry is converted into an Alpaca-style prompt that combines a fixed introductory template with the instruction, the input when present, and the response from the dataset output.

When batching tokenized prompts, shorter sequences are padded within each batch to the length of the longest sequence using token ID 50256, the end-of-text token, so all rows have the same number of token positions.
